body:
REVIEWER DISPOSITION ON THE THREE SPEC DECISIONS: ACCEPT all three, with six binding amendments. Evidence is exact main c8ffe86.

1. OWNERSHIP: ACCEPT. acquire may own the renderer-independent SourceIdentities, TargetUniverse, acquisition/stage outcomes, and invocation account; view may own projection/report outcomes, provenance-derived ViewBasis, and the composed result; codec may own canonical encoders; StoryAtlas may own files and browser lowering. I rechecked build.sbt: codec -> view is acyclic because view does not depend on codec. It is still a new module edge and a build.sbt edit, so it needs the chief ADR ruling and coordination announcement before implementation. Core StorySource remains core; acquire owns only the output/account aggregate that refers to it.

2. canonical.txt: ACCEPT, and make its condition exact. The role is present whenever a StorySource was successfully constructed, independent of semantic resolution and independent of every report outcome. If acquisition fails before StorySource construction it is absent and that absence is accounted by the acquisition outcome. StorySource.fromText cannot succeed without canonicalText, so whenever canonicalization succeeds is otherwise too vague.

3. OFFSET AND CHECKSUM LAW: canonical_source bytes are strict UTF-8, no BOM and no added newline, and their SHA-256 must equal StorySource.canonicalChecksum as produced by Checksum.ofText. The manifest/result must also state that every TextSpan is zero-based half-open UTF-16 CODE UNITS after strict UTF-8 decoding, not UTF-8 byte offsets and not Unicode code points. Record both byte length and UTF-16 length or derive and verify them. Add an astral-character court before a supported span; ASCII-only fixtures cannot catch this coordinate error.

4. THREE IDENTITIES: source.txt may preserve original input bytes, while canonical.txt preserves the coordinate string, but SourceIdentities must separately bind: original byte checksum plus media type; decoder identity/charset and decoded rawText checksum; canonical checksum plus storysource-canonical-text/v1. Never infer identity equality merely because two digests happen to match. A CRLF plus BOM plus trailing-tab court should show raw bytes, decoded StorySource.rawText, and canonicalText staying distinct while each remains reproducible.

5. TWO ROOTS: ACCEPT result.json story-output-result/v1 and manifest.json story-output-manifest/v1. The StoryModel member must be encoded by the existing StoryModelCodec canonical encoder, not copied into a second family of fields. The manifest correctly omits its self-checksum; define BundleId as the checksum of canonical manifest bytes derived by the consumer or outer container, never a recursive field. Every promised non-manifest role needs exactly one role, portable relative path, media type, byte length, checksum, and required/conditional status.

6. FAIL CLOSED WITHOUT LOSING VALID CORE: an unknown root schema version or unknown closed core tag fails decoding that root. An unknown extension envelope must not be interpreted as accepted, but it should become a typed UnsupportedExtension outcome carrying namespace, schema id, checksum, and requiredness while known core and a valid StoryModel remain available. If that extension was required by a requested report, that report outcome is Unsupported or Failed. Do not turn an optional future extension into loss of an otherwise auditable partial delivery.

Minimum added courts beyond the draft list: report lowering fails while canonical.txt and the semantic result remain intact; astral UTF-16 coordinate roundtrip; raw BOM/CRLF/trailing-tab three-identity separation; mutate/delete canonical.txt; unknown optional extension preserves core but is not accepted; unknown required extension accounts the report as unsupported; StoryModel member decode/encode bytes equal StoryModelCodec canonical bytes.

With these amendments I support cutting the child bead at docs/design/story-output-bundle-spec.md and freezing the normative spec before implementation. No path, staffing, dependency, or implementation authority is implied by this review.
